name: Lime Yellow
lede: Lime Yellow is a vivid, green-leaning yellow, bright enough to sit on the border between yellow and green.

sections.title: A dictionary yellow
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines lime yellow as a medium yellow or greenish yellow [1]. It appears in his yellows list beside lime, lemon yellow and light straw [2]. The same dictionary keeps separate entries for lime white, the color of calcium oxide or lime, and for limestone, a brownish grey [1]. Those belong to the mineral, not to this color.

The swatch here is much stronger than a dictionary's "medium" yellow. Our records give it a chroma of 96, which is very intense for a screen color [3]. It also has an ISCC-NBS 1955 entry (block 87), and Wikipedia cites Crayola for the name [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The name has close twins in our records: Neon Yellow, Arctic Lime and Volt all sit within a ΔE of 1.5 of this swatch [3]. Its nearest standard neighbor is [[lime]], 2.5 ΔE away [3]. Related names: [[lime-green]], [[chartreuse]], [[green-yellow]] and [[lemon-yellow]].
